suffices h : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ xs ys : List α, xs.length + ys.length = n →
      (interleave xs ys).length = xs.length + ys.length from h _ xs ys rfl
  intro n
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    intro xs ys hn
    cases xs with
    | nil => simp [interleave]
    | cons x xs =>
      simp only [interleave, List.length_cons] at hn ⊢
      have := ih (ys.length + xs.length) (by omega) ys xs rfl
      simp only [List.length_cons] at this ⊢
      omega

**The proof** (strong induction on the total length):

theorem length_interleave (xs ys : List α) :

  suffices h : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ xs ys : List α, xs.length + ys.length = n →
      (interleave xs ys).length = xs.length + ys.length from h _ xs ys rfl
  intro n
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    intro xs ys hn
    cases xs with
    | nil => simp [interleave]
    | cons x xs =>

      have := ih (ys.length + xs.length) (by omega) ys xs rfl
      omega
```

Why this shape: the recursive call `interleave ys xs` swaps the arguments, so induction on `xs` alone doesn't work. The total length `xs.length + ys.length` strictly decreases on the recursive call, which is what the induction uses.

I checked the logic by reading it, not by running it. The most likely failure points are the `simp only [interleave, ...]` unfolding step and the `omega` calls. If you can get a working `lean` on this machine, run the check and send me any errors.
